assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a lipid self-assembly and phase-behaviour problem solved in practice: pH-dependent charge, nucleic-acid encapsulation, and fusogenic non-bilayer structure make delivery of fragile RNA possible. Impact is very large and chemically clear (siRNA therapy, mRNA vaccines), and it is close to my own field of lipid-water physical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (including Hope) built the formulation and ionizable-lipid concept; Anderson and Langer developed combinatorial lipid libraries. Credit is spread over a decade of academic and industrial work, with MacLachlan and Madden also central, so a three-person selection leaves out real contributors.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven at global scale and independently reproduced across several lipid chemistries, so the field is mature. Timing is good, since the 2023 Medicine prize covered nucleoside modification, not the carrier.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as pharmaceutical technology
Allocation among Cullis, MacLachlan, Madden, Hope, Anderson and Langer is contested
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may reduce appetite

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle of the cell recast intracellular compartmentation in physical-chemical terms (condensates, P granules, nucleoli). The concept is original and has opened new directions in cell biology, neurodegeneration and soft-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P-granule liquid behaviour; Rosen supplied the multivalent-interaction framework with reconstituted systems. Pappu and Mittag contributed theory and sequence grammar. A Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen trio is defensible but leaves out the polymer-physics side.
assessment.maturity: Rapid growth and strong independent confirmation in vitro, but ongoing debate about how far in vitro droplets reflect in vivo function and what counts as phase separation, so interpretation is still settling.
uncertainties: Functional relevance of condensates in living cells is still debated
Credit between cell biologists and physical chemists is unresolved
Possible tension between premature and timely recognition

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turned induced proximity into a general therapeutic chemistry: bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues hijack E3 ligases to remove proteins. It is conceptually original, widely adopted and now in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched PROTACs, with Crews also central to the VHL-recruiting compounds; Ciulli contributed structure-guided design. The thalidomide-cereblon glue work of Handa and Ito is a separate branch, so the compound discovery may need different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups and many clinical candidates, but no PROTAC drug has been fully approved yet, so the long-term clinical payoff is not settled.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug as of my knowledge
Allocation between PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages
Whether Handa, Ito, Gray and Sakamoto should be included

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cell efficiencies from a few percent to over 25 percent in about a decade, driven by solid-state chemistry (composition, defects, interfaces). The scientific and technological impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park the first solid-state cell with long-lived operation, and Snaith the thin-film planar and mixed-halide improvements. Grätzel, Kanatzidis and Seok also have strong claims, so a three-name selection is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency records are confirmed across many laboratories, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial scale-up are not resolved, so recognition may be a little early.
uncertainties: Long-term device stability remains unproven
Fair attribution among six strong claimants
Commercial deployment still limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing links membrane-protein engineering and single-molecule electrochemistry to a practical DNA and RNA reading technology. It is original, has had broad impact in genomics, and rests on lipid-bilayer and protein-pore physical chemistry that I know well.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Akeson conceived strand sequencing; Kasianowicz showed polynucleotide passage through alpha-hemolysin; Bayley engineered pores and enzyme-based readout. Branton died in 2020, so only living candidates can be proposed.
assessment.maturity: Commercial instruments have been in wide use for over a decade and are independently validated, so maturity is high. Accuracy has improved, though lingering concerns about error rates limit some applications.
uncertainties: Credit among early conceptual and later engineering contributions is contested
Whether the prize would be seen as analytical chemistry or biophysics

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pairs allows site-specific incorporation of non-canonical amino acids in living cells. It is a clear and original chemical-biology invention with wide use in protein engineering.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the first general approach in E. coli and yeast, Wang contributed early methods, and Chin extended it to multicellular organisms and genome-scale recoding. Yokoyama and Mehl also have credible claims.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely applied; applications in therapeutics are still emerging. Recognition could be timely.
uncertainties: Medicine and Chemistry overlap with synthetic-biology prizes
Allocation among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama
Limited expertise of mine in this area

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory and the funnel picture explain how proteins fold quickly and reproducibly despite huge conformational space. This is a core physical-chemistry concept with deep influence on protein biophysics and self-assembly.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the main authors of the funnel formalism, with Bryngelson; Dill contributed hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model ideas, and Fersht experimental mapping. The theory-versus-experiment split makes the credit complicated.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are broadly accepted and tested experimentally, and structure prediction by AI has partly overshadowed the framework, which may affect how recognition is seen. Timing is arguably late rather than early.
uncertainties: Whether the committee still sees folding theory as a distinct prize-worthy discovery after the 2024 prize
Attribution between theorists and experimentalists
Distance from my own research area

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer links charge transfer and proton motion in enzymes, photosynthesis and molecular catalysis. The theory and the physical-organic experiments give a unifying mechanistic framework with importance for fuel-forming and energy chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Hammes-Schiffer developed the theoretical framework, Mayer the thermochemical concept of bond-dissociation free energies and concerted PCET, Nocera model systems and catalysis. Meyer, a pioneer, is also credible.
assessment.maturity: Concept is mature and widely used; it is a broad framework more than a single discovery, so the prize motivation would need careful definition.
uncertainties: Is a unifying framework rather than a single discovery
Credit across theory, kinetics and catalysis
Limited overlap with my own expertise
